definitions.explanation: A small adhesive bandage for cuts and scrapes. The name is a Johnson & Johnson brand, used by many speakers for any such bandage.

examples.english: To put a Band-Aid on one's finger.

examples.japanese: ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{指|ゆび}→指：01518_yubi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}った→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、バンドエイド⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I cut my finger on some paper, so someone gave me a Band-Aid.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{転|ころ}ぶ→転ぶ：00863_korobu⟧たび⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦キャラクター→キャラクター：23518_kyarakutaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{絵|え}→絵：02613_e⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついたバンドエイド⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}って→貼る：10447_haru⟧ほし⟦がる→〜がる：03089_garu⟧。
examples.english: Every time the child falls over, they want a Band-Aid with a cartoon character on it.

notes:
The general word is ⟦{絆創膏|ばんそうこう}→絆創膏：05386_bansoukou⟧. Which brand name people use for it varies by region: バンドエイド in many areas, カットバン, サビオ or リバテープ in others, a well-known difference in Japanese dialect geography.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- バンドエイド⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}る→貼る：10447_haru⟧: to put on a Band-Aid
- バンドエイド⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はがす: to take off a Band-Aid
